machine.virtualisation: Docker Desktop LinuxKit VM; existing physical-host workloads left running; not isolated bare-metal Linux performance

method.transport: UDP ChannelData over loopback in both directions
method.synchronisation: All server readiness probes finish at a barrier before loaders launch. Each loader independently performs allocation setup, warm-up and sequential latency before its throughput phase.
method.aggregate_timing: Estimate each phase end from its flushed result-line arrival, then subtract the loader-reported elapsed seconds for phase start. Aggregate rate divides all delivered packets by the enclosing interval across all process phases; it is not the sum of individual rates. Pipe/scheduling delay adds uncertainty. Overlap fraction is recorded; inspect low overlap before drawing conclusions.
method.limits: Separately addressed processes with evenly partitioned allocations, client load workers and disjoint UDP relay-port ranges (to avoid cross-process port reuse). This does not implement shared-port multiworker support, request distribution, failover, maximum sustainable capacity or WAN acceptance. Each process has its own load-generator process and echo peers. Default per-process resource limits are retained, so aggregate configured server quotas increase with process count. CPU includes the complete server lifetime; RSS peaks and quiescent kernel socket snapshots are per process, not simultaneous total-memory measurements. Same-host generators and VM scheduling may limit scaling.
method.spry_variant: Same-source default binary preserved and SHA-verified against the full Linux comparison before portable rebuild; no server multiworker feature was added.

kernel_socket_memory.method: ss -m -e attributed by process-owned /proc fd socket inodes
kernel_socket_memory.limits: Point-in-time counters are not additive total kernel memory; rb/tb are configured buffer ceilings, not allocated bytes. Socket structs/slabs, unreported sockets and missed peaks are excluded.
